title: bug(daemon): a wrapper_restart deregister releases the reloading seat's held task at once; hold it for the relaunch for settings.reloadHoldMs (default 2 min)
description:
Daemon slice of task-f81c85acfec54b0f89affccb7a833b6a (a wrapper hot reload hands a mid-step row to a peer). That row keeps the human DoD, depends on this one, and owns the postflight arms and the docs. Split because the whole change is about 12 files, over the 10-file plan cap.

WHY. Both launchers' hot reload sends moe.deregister_worker {reason:"wrapper_restart"} and then re-execs (sh `exec`, ps1 in-process supervisor). deregisterWorker (state/workerLifecycle.ts) releases every task at once and marks the seat DEAD, so the row is claimable in the seconds before the re-exec'd wrapper's first claim. Activity log 11-01..11-03: the relaunch re-claimed its row 2.4-8.5 s after the deregister; three times an idle peer won inside 1.7-2.4 s (WT-14 task-befdddf7 at 23:07:18Z on 11-02, 3ad573a7 at 01:55:27Z on 11-03, dd1ee586 at 09:55:58Z on 11-02).

DELIVERABLE
1. Hold. deregisterWorker with reason exactly "wrapper_restart", for a record that is not DEAD and holds at least one active task (getActiveTasksAssignedToWorker: PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW/BLOCKED), with a resolved reloadHoldMs above 0. closeOwnFinalizingAttempts still runs first, unchanged. Then it releases nothing and leaves the assignment, the attempt, the worker status, resource claims and chat cursors alone. It writes worker.reloadHoldUntil (ISO, now + reloadHoldMs), posts one 🔌 banner to #workers and #governors naming the held tasks and the deadline, appends WORKER_DISCONNECTED {workerId, reason, releasedTaskIds: [], heldTaskIds, holdUntil}, and returns the held ids and holdUntil. A repeat wrapper_restart during a hold returns the same holdUntil with no new banner, activity row or write: a hold never extends itself. Any other reason, a seat holding no active task, or reloadHoldMs 0 runs today's flow unchanged, and its DEAD write also sets reloadHoldUntil null.
2. Peers. No claim-path change: the record stays non-DEAD and assigned, so isTaskClaimable is false. The ranked pool skips the row, an explicit-taskId claim is refused as already assigned, and replaceExisting stays the explicit takeover.
3. Return. moe.claim_next_task from the held workerId clears reloadHoldUntil (updateWorker) after refreshWorkerType and before the one-task-per-worker check, so that same call answers alreadyAssigned for the held task and the wrapper resumes it. Nothing else ends a hold (join_team, chat and heartbeat do not).
4. Expiry. A mutex-wrapped reload-hold sweep runs from the stale-worker watcher's 60 s interval, before checkStaleWorkers (which returns early when no governor is online). For each record whose reloadHoldUntil does not parse or is at or before now, it calls deregisterWorker(state, id, "reload_hold_expired"), which is today's full release: nextStatusForRelease routing, attempt close, DEAD, releaseOnDeregister drops, chat-leave lines and the banner. Per-record try/catch: a failure is logged and the pass continues. A dead reload's row is therefore released between reloadHoldMs and reloadHoldMs + 60 s after the reload.
5. Setting. settings.reloadHoldMs (ProjectSettings in types/schema.ts), resolved at use time: absent, or not a finite number of at least 0, gives 120000 (2 min); 0 disables the hold; a value above 1800000 is capped at 1800000. Worker gains optional reloadHoldUntil?: string | null (absent means no hold), so existing .moe/ records load unchanged. A restart keeps the persisted deadline, and the first sweep after load enforces it.
6. Response. deregister_worker adds heldTaskIds (always; [] when nothing is held) and holdUntil (only on a hold), keeps every existing field, and its description names the hold. The /ws DEREGISTER_WORKER ack is unchanged (JetBrains sends "terminal_closed").

NOT IN SCOPE: scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 (the reload already sends wrapper_restart, and a landing that changes either file hot-reloads every seat); the postflight arms; docs/MCP_SERVER.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, docs/SCHEMA.md and scripts/CLAUDE.md (task-f81c85ac owns them); any idle-based release.

VERIFICATION (the full daemon suite, because types/schema.ts changes), from the task worktree: S=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-reload-hold-XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S" && for f in <owned paths>; do cp "$f" "$S/$f"; done && cd "$S/packages/moe-daemon" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" NO_COLOR=1 bash -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npx vitest run'
definitionOfDone: A vitest case in the new packages/moe-daemon/src/state/reloadHold.test.ts: a seat that claimed a WORKING task deregisters with reason wrapper_restart. The response has heldTaskIds [that task], releasedTaskIds [] and a holdUntil; the task stays assigned to the seat and WORKING, its attempt stays running, and the worker is not DEAD.

A vitest case: during that hold a peer's ranked claim_next_task answers hasNext:false and its explicit-taskId claim is refused as already assigned; the same workerId's next claim_next_task answers alreadyAssigned with that task and leaves reloadHoldUntil null.

A vitest case: with no claim from the seat, a reload-hold sweep before holdUntil changes nothing, and one after it leaves the task, its attempt and the worker in the same state a terminal_closed deregister produces; a peer's claim then gets the task.

Vitest cases: reloadHoldMs absent gives 120000, 0 releases at once as today, a value above 1800000 is capped at 1800000, and a negative or non-number value gives 120000; a deregister with any other reason during a hold releases at once.

The full daemon suite passes in a Linux snapshot (npm ci, tsc --noEmit, vitest run), with the existing chatSystemFeed, joinTeam.deadMembers, joinTeam.notification, workerType, resourceStore.deregister and reattachAttempt tests unchanged.
taskRails: Do not edit scripts/moe-agent.sh or scripts/moe-agent.ps1 in this row: every landing that changes either file hot-reloads the whole fleet, and the live daemon still releases on wrapper_restart until it is rebuilt.
